propositions: The gate matches field names globally as bare attribute strings, allowing an inert field to pass if any unrelated config declares a same-named attribute, creating a false-negative class for common field names like enabled, path, timeout, remote, branch, mode.
A field is satisfied only when a read resolves to the owning dataclass that declares it, not when the bare attribute name appears anywhere in the codebase.

Four newly-flagged fields (McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure) were traced to real consumers via indirect reads excluded from the gate's plumbing-file exemptions or string-keyed access patterns.

Receiver resolution must bind reads through six patterns: section-attribute names, parameter/variable annotations, local alias assignments, function return annotations, control-flow branches, and cross-module call-site propagation.
Existing test files must migrate to the owner-resolution contract and invert the defect-pinning test that currently documents bare-name collision as an accepted trade-off.
Accurate read-via markers must be added for the four newly-flagged fields citing their real consumers, and any marker naming a closed ticket ID must be reported.
